knowledge_used.how_applied: Thermal-budget method P_max = (T_J,max - T_A)/(R_thJC + R_iso + 2 R_hs) reused with ambient raised from TI's 40 degC to 50 degC and a parametric pad resistance (0.1-0.5 K/W); TI's warning that TIDA-010054 is intended for room ambient only drives the explicit 50 degC verification point (A-18) and the chamber/extrapolation item in the test approach (A-37). Fan airflow/aux-rail consideration drives A-19/A-22.

P_max sensitivity 57.3 W -> 52.1 W per device when T_A goes from 40 to 50 degC (R_thJC 0.42, R_iso 0.5, R_hs 0.5 K/W, parametric); basis for accepting the 50 degC ambient seed with a 9 % budget penalty.
Both TO-247-4 devices on one shared heat sink with a rated insulating pad (A-16); pad resistance carried in the thermal budget; pad voltage rating is a human-review item.
Firmware scope A-34: NTC/heat-sink temperature is cooling supervision, not junction protection; fan-failure detection flagged (A-19).

Principle 1 (isolate every position) and principle 2 (Kelvin-source reference) define the SELV isolation concept A-21 and the one-TO-247-4-per-position arrangement A-16; principle 3 / KR-GD-001 make the selected device datasheet, not PRD-04814 numbers, govern gate levels (A-17).

A synchronous buck is a half bridge with complementary switching, so the negative turn-off recommendation applies even though PRD-04814 lists the buck among single-ended topologies where 0 V may be used; decision handed to the gate-driver agent (A-17).
Dead time is generated by the F28335 dead-band module (initial 200 ns, 2 % of period, about 2.2 W body-diode loss at 27.5 A); the interlock is only a last barrier; both-inputs-high test is in A-37.

DESAT trip must stay above the corrected 31.6 A overload peak over temperature; reference values (6.4 V/1 us, 6.7 V/46 ns) are not copied; derivation and measurement are surfaced for the gate-driver agent and reviewer (A-10, A-15).

Applicability depends on the board partition: differential PWM/fault (CB-GD-003) if drivers and controller are on separate boards, buffered single-ended with RC filters on one board (rule exclusion). Register A-21 is written to be compatible with both outcomes.

The skill excludes inductor-defined output filters, so the output ripple requirement A-09 uses C >= dI_L/(8 fs dV) and ESR <= dV/dI_L instead of the dQ method; the dQ method (KR-CAP-001) is noted as applicable to the pulsed buck input current for the capacitor agent; principle 4 (TI states no derating rule) is cited for A-04.
Applies to the input DC-link (pulsed current, I_Cin,rms 12.4-13.75 A); not used for the output filter.
Output capacitor RMS current dI_L/sqrt(12) = 2.4 A and input capacitor RMS 12.4-13.75 A must be within rating at 50 kHz and the hot-spot temperature assumed in A-29.
Two-tier film plus local HV ceramics recorded as the layout assumption behind the EMC scope (A-28) and the PE-PCB-002/003 constraints.
No transformer; no DC-blocking capacitor.
Phase-shift/DAB soft-switching boundary does not exist in a hard-switched buck.

Gate-power budget (KR-IS-001) evaluated for 118 nC, 19 V, 50 kHz = 0.11 W per device; module quiescent power dominates the 12 V budget (A-22). KR-IS-003/KR-IS-002 define the EMI-aware scope A-28. KR-IS-004 (bias sharing) is a human-review item for the gate-driver agent.
Q_G * fs * (V_DD - V_EE) computed; shows gate power is negligible in the auxiliary budget.
Protection scope A-35: hardware short-circuit protection per switch is required because this is a complete prototype, not an evaluation fixture (rule exclusion does not apply).
Latched combined fault with UVLO lock-out required (A-35); converter-level UVLO ladder A-02 uses the same lock-out logic.

Auxiliary 12 V input must be protected (reverse polarity, OVP, UVLO consistent with bias-converter input range) - A-22; CB-PR-001 pattern cited, part choice left to the auxiliary agent (CMP-TPS2640 unverified here).

KR-SN-001 and KR-SN-002 applied directly (isolation rating, divider headroom >= 1.1 x 480 V input, >= 1.25 x 200 V output); KR-SN-003 not applicable because the F28335 has no SDFM; KR-SN-005 fast hardware OC path required; Lab 2 stepwise commissioning practice shapes A-37.
Delta-sigma bitstream sensing needs an SDFM peripheral; the TMS320F28335 has none, so analog isolated amplifiers / Hall sensors to the ADC are assumed.

PCB constraints hand-off: isolation keep-outs on all layers (KR-ISO-001), net classes (KR-ISO-003), slots >= 1 mm (KR-ISO-004), V_GS probe points (KR-PCB-005) recorded in A-33/A-37 and pcb_constraints.
Environmental inputs for the standards agent fixed: CTI >= 175 V (group IIIa, Isola 370HR class 3 verified), pollution degree 2, altitude <= 2000 m, OVC II (A-25..A-27, A-30).
70 um copper on every power-board layer with paralleled pours and via arrays (A-31); PE-PCB-006 evidence requirement noted.
EMI-aware layout scope A-28 and the control/power separation assumptions reference the project rules; acceptance evidence remains human review per docs/pcb-design-rules.md.

Decision 1: 700-800 V operating window compared with the +/-10 % seed; decision 8: 12 V aux protection pattern; decision 9: 40 degC thermal model and room-ambient warning; decision 10: 300 x 180 mm at 10 kW as a size benchmark for the mechanical envelope. Instance values (2 ohm, 6.4 V/1 us, 45/70 A, 60 uF) explicitly not copied.

Decision 1 gate-level guidance (+15 V, -3 to -4 V, maxima +19/-8 V) cited as method; the selected device datasheet governs (KR-GD-001); its single-ended 0 V note is overridden by the half-bridge nature of the synchronous buck (KR-GD-005).
Decision 7 observed PCB practice (Tg >= 170 degC, ENIG, 1 mm non-plated slots) supports the laminate and slot assumptions A-30/A-33; its 8 mm creepage is not generalised.

Decision 4 differential signalling with fail-safe polarity and interlock becomes a conditional requirement if the architecture agent separates driver and control boards (A-21); decision 2 DESAT values not copied.

# Design assumptions register - 400 V to 200 V, 5 kW, 50 kHz SiC synchronous buck (V2)

AI-GENERATED ENGINEERING PROTOTYPE V2 - HUMAN REVIEW REQUIRED. This register was produced by the assumptions agent from the task text (task09102026.txt), the orchestrator design-basis seeds and the AIPE Engineering Knowledge System. Insulation coordination (insulation class, clearance, creepage, test voltages) is supplied by the standards agent in its own section; this register only states the environmental inputs that section needs (A-25 to A-27).

## 1. Requirements versus assumptions - "Do not silently invent specifications"

The user fixed nine quantities (Section 2). Every other number in this document is an engineering choice made so that the design can proceed. None of it is a user requirement, none of it has been confirmed by the user, and a reviewer may change any of it without invalidating the user requirements. Four classes are used throughout the V2 example:

- USER REQUIREMENT (U): given in the task; not negotiable by any agent.
- AGENT-SELECTED ASSUMPTION (S): a value the task leaves open, proposed by the orchestrator as a seed and reviewed here. S* marks a seed this register corrects; the corrected value is the design value.
- AGENT-DERIVED VALUE (D): follows arithmetically from U and S values and changes automatically when its inputs change.
- HUMAN REVIEW (H): an item this agent must not decide; it is surfaced with a proposal and must be closed by a person.

Rule applied by every downstream agent: a quantity that is absent from the task and from this register is unspecified; no calculation, schematic note or BOM comment may treat it as a requirement. Reference-design instance values (TIDA-010054 2 ohm gate resistors, 6.4 V / 1 us DESAT, 45 A / 70 A Hall trips, 20 uF rail decoupling; CGD1700HB2M-UNA 1 ohm / 6.7 V / 46 ns) are not design values for this converter and are cited only as method examples (REF-TI-TIDA-010054 "what AIPE should not generalise"; SKILL-001 known limitations).

## 2. User requirements (class U)

| ID | Quantity | Value | Drives |

## 3. Operating-point table (class D)

Equations (ideal CCM buck, plain text): D = Vout / Vin; Iin,ideal = Pout / Vin; Iin,98 = Pout / (0.98 * Vin); dI_L = Vout * (1 - D) / (L * fs) with L = 267 uH (seed) and fs = 50 kHz; I_pk = Io + dI_L / 2; I_L,rms = sqrt(Io^2 + dI_L^2 / 12); I_Cin,rms = Io * sqrt(D * (1 - D)) (ripple neglected). D_eff with losses in series is about D / 0.98 (0.567 / 0.510 / 0.464).

## 6. How these assumptions differ from V1 (48 V / 1 kW) and why

| Topic | V1 | V2 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Input range | 36-54 V (+/-25 %, battery-like bus) | 360-440 V (+/-10 %) with a UVLO / OVP / survival ladder | A 400 V regulated bus is not a battery; a +/-25 % window would force 300-500 V device and capacitor stress for no stated reason |
| Hazard and isolation | Shared control/power ground, non-isolated bootstrap driver (SKILL-001 scope exclusion) | Isolated SELV control domain; isolated drivers, bias supplies and sensors | 400 V and 200 V are hazardous; every barrier part is rated for the working voltage (KR-SN-001) |
| Switching frequency | 100 kHz (agent choice) | 50 kHz (user requirement) | User requirement; it also lowers the switching loss of the hard-switched SiC leg |
| Current levels | 41.7 A output, 21-28 A input | 25 A output, 11.4-15.6 A input | Power quadrupled but voltages are 8 times higher; copper per ampere is less demanding, insulation far more |
| Ripple and L | 10 uH, ripple set by 100 kHz | 267 uH, 30 % ripple | Scales with Vout (1 - D) / (dI fs) |
| Load transient | 20 A / 100 us illustrative, no dynamic specification | 12.5 A step, +/-5 %, 5 ms as a design specification | The task asks for transient operating conditions to be assumed explicitly |
| Ambient / cooling | 0-50 degC, forced air, external insulated heat sink | Same, with an explicit 50 degC verification point, >= 2 m/s and a fan current budget | Thermal design must influence placement (task section 13); TIDA-010054's 40 degC model and room-ambient warning were reviewed |
| Efficiency | None stated | >= 98 % target, 97.5 % floor | The task asks for an efficiency target |
| Board | 300 x 220 mm, six layers, mixed 70/35 um | Power board 2-4 layers 70 um, control board 4 layers 35 um, partition chosen by the architecture agent | Task preference for lower layer counts and compactness; isolation drives the partition |
| Protection | Comparators plus latch, not a hard-short interrupter | DESAT-class hardware protection per switch, latched combined fault | SiC short-circuit withstand is microseconds (KR-PR-001) |
| Auxiliary | Derived from the 48 V input on board | External 12 V SELV supply, <= 2 A | A 400 V to 12 V converter on board would add an isolated supply outside the benchmark scope |

## 7. Knowledge applicability summary

Direct: SKILL-001 principle 1 (A-21); SKILL-006 principle 1 and KR-TH-001 (A-18); KR-TH-002 (A-16); KR-TH-003 (A-34); KR-SN-001 and KR-ISO-001 (A-21); KR-ISO-002/003/004 (A-26, A-30, A-33); KR-PR-001/002/003 (A-35, A-22); KR-SN-002 (A-03, A-36); KR-SN-005 (A-35); KR-GD-009 (A-17, A-37); KR-PCB-006 and PE-PCB-006 (A-31); KR-CAP-002 (A-09 output-capacitor RMS); KR-IS-001 (A-22); CB-PR-001 (A-22 pattern). Adapted: SKILL-003 (the dQ method applies to the buck input capacitor, whose current is pulsed, not to the output filter; the ripple equation is used instead); KR-CAP-001/003 (input side, capacitor agent); KR-GD-005 (a synchronous buck is a half bridge with complementary switching, so the half-bridge recommendation applies although PRD-04814 lists the buck as single-ended; decision with the gate-driver agent); KR-GD-008 (depends on the partition); the SKILL-006 thermal model (ambient changed from 40 to 50 degC, pad resistance parametric). Not applicable: KR-SN-003 (the F28335 has no SDFM); KR-CAP-004 and KR-PE-001 (no transformer, no phase-shift converter); the SKILL-004 bootstrap exclusion is irrelevant (isolated bias chosen). Human review: KR-GD-004 trip derivation; KR-IS-004 bias sharing; KR-TH-002 pad rating; PE strategy (A-23); 50 degC verification (A-37).
